title: [Bug] ttnn.from_torch to an integer dtype disagrees with the device, differently on x86_64 and aarch64: the host static_cast is undefined behaviour
body:
### Describe the bug **Host float-to-integer conversion is undefined behaviour on both architectures this repository builds for, and it disagrees with the device on both.** Which one is wrong depends on the destination dtype. `tt_metal/impl/tensor/tensor_apis.cpp:484`, inside `transform_buffers()`, converts every element with an unchecked cast: ```cpp std::transform(data.begin(), data.end(), output_vector.begin(), [](SrcType value) { return static_cast(value); }); ``` A floating-to-integral `static_cast` whose value is outside the destination's range is undefined behaviour in C++, and the two architectures this repo builds for resolve it differently: x86 `cvttss2si` yields `INT_MIN` for anything out of range including `+inf` and NaN, while aarch64 `fcvtzs` saturates and maps NaN to `0`. This is reached from `ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=...)`, `ttnn.to_dtype`, host `ttnn.typecast`, and `Tensor::from_span` / `from_vector` (`host_tensor_factory.cpp:51,111`, both of which end in `return to_dtype(res, spec.data_type())`). Source dtypes FLOAT32, BFLOAT16, BFLOAT8_B, BFLOAT4_B; destinations UINT8, INT8, UINT16, UINT32, INT32. ### Observed vs expected I compiled the lambda above unmodified and ran it **natively on aarch64**, and on **x86_64 under emulation** (gcc 12.5 in a `linux/amd64` container on that same aarch64 host). The device column is what the SFPU kernel selects, read from `ckernel_sfpu_typecast.h:194` for int32 and `:246-260` for uint32. | input | x86_64 host | aarch64 host | device | |---|---|---|---| | `1e30` to INT32 | -2147483648 | **+2147483647** | -2147483648 | | `NaN` to INT32 | -2147483648 | **0** | -2147483648 | | `+inf` to UINT32 | **0** | 4294967295 | 4294967295 | | `-1.0` to UINT32 | **4294967295** | 0 | 0 | | `-3e9` to UINT32 | **1294967296** | 0 | 0 | | bf16 max finite `3.39e38` to INT32 | -2147483648 | **+2147483647** | -2147483648 | | `4.2e9` to UINT16 | **0** | 59904 | n/a | **The polarity flips by destination dtype.** For INT32 the x86 host agrees with silicon and ARM does not. For UINT32 the ARM host agrees with silicon and **x86 does not**: on x86, `ttnn.from_torch(tensor_containing_minus_3e9, dtype=ttnn.uint32)` gives `1294967296` where the device gives `0`, and `+inf` gives `0` where the device saturates to `4294967295`. So there are two separate host/device disagreements, one on each architecture, and neither can be dismissed as an unsupported-platform issue. ### Why no test catches it The golden carries the same undefined behaviour, so it moves with the implementation instead of checking it: ```mermaid flowchart LR IMPL["implementation
tensor_apis.cpp:484
static_cast<DstType>(value)"] GOLD["golden
core.py:249
torch.clamp(x.to(torch.int32), 0, 65535)"] UB{{"out-of-range float to int
is undefined behaviour"}} X86["on x86_64
both yield INT_MIN"] ARM["on aarch64
both saturate"] PASS(["comparison passes
on both hosts"]) DEV["device SFPU
one fixed answer per dtype"] BUG(["host and device disagree,
differently per architecture"]) IMPL --> UB GOLD --> UB UB --> X86 --> PASS UB --> ARM --> PASS IMPL -.compared against.-> DEV DEV --> BUG style PASS fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a style BUG fill:#fee2e2,stroke:#dc2626 style UB fill:#fef9c3,stroke:#ca8a04 ``` The inner `.to(torch.int32)` in the golden is the same out-of-range conversion the bug is about. `ttnn/ttnn/operations/core.py:249`: ```python torch.clamp(input_tensor.to(torch.int32), 0, 65535) ``` The inner `.to(torch.int32)` is the same out-of-range conversion, so golden and implementation move together per architecture and both stay green while returning different numbers on different hosts. The same shape appears at `core.py:611`, `:626` and `:630`. Separately, `tests/ttnn/python_api_testing/typecast_test_helpers.py:47` only widens to `out_max + 80000`, nowhere near `2^31`. And `.github/workflows/build-aarch64-native.yaml` builds but runs **no tests**, so nothing on the aarch64 side is exercised in CI at all. ### The fix pattern already exists in this repo `tt_metal/impl/tensor/host_to_tensor_spec_apis.cpp:44-60` has `validate_float_pad_against_integral()`, which converts to `double`, asserts `std::isfinite`, and range-checks against `std::numeric_limits::lowest()` and `::max()` before casting. It is applied to the scalar pad value and not to the bulk element conversion one file away. Two defensible target behaviours, and the choice is yours rather than mine: **saturate**, matching `torch.Tensor.to()` and both test goldens, or **reject** with `TT_FATAL`, matching the existing validator. A bulk tensor conversion that starts rejecting would break code that currently works by accident, so saturation looks right for `to_dtype` even if rejection is right for a user-supplied scalar. ### Nine more sites in the pad family, and one outside it Same mechanism, user-supplied value. Measured on the verbatim expressions: | `pad_value` | dtype | x86_64 | aarch64 | |---|---|---|---| | `-1.0` | UINT32 | `0xFFFFFFFF` | **0** | | `-1.0` | UINT16 | `0xFFFF` | **0** | | `-32768.0` | UINT16 | `0x8000` | **0** | | `+inf` | UINT32 | **0** | `0xFFFFFFFF` | | `3e9` | INT32 | -2147483648 | **+2147483647** | `ttnn.pad(uint32_index_tensor, ..., value=-1)`, the usual invalid-index sentinel, writes `0xFFFFFFFF` on x86 and `0` on ARM. **`0` is a valid index**, so on ARM this silently corrupts data rather than marking it. Three sites cast explicitly: - `data_movement/fill_pad/device/fill_pad_program_factory.hpp:65,66,67` - `data_movement/tilize_with_val_padding/device/factories/tilize_with_val_padding_factory_helper.cpp:27,35,43` - `data_movement/pad/device/pad_rm_sharded_width_only_program_factory.cpp:120` Six more convert implicitly with no cast at all, all under `data_movement/pad/device/`: `pad_tile_program_factory.cpp:80`, `pad_tile_multicore_program_factory.cpp:93`, `pad_rm_reader_writer_program_factory.cpp:92`, `pad_rm_reader_writer_multi_core_program_factory.cpp:254`, `pad_rm_reader_writer_multi_core_default_program_factory.cpp:109`, `pad_rm_sharded_height_only_program_factory.cpp:341`. **`ttnn.pad` picks its factory by memory layout, so fixing some and not others makes an out-of-range pad behave differently depending on the tensor's layout.** All seven need the same change together. `experimental/quasar` mirrors the family (seven pad factories plus its own `tilize_with_val_padding_factory_helper.cpp:27,35,43`) and would need it too. Outside the pad family, `eltwise/ternary/device/ternary_op_utils.cpp:423` does `std::bit_cast(static_cast(scalar))` on a float scalar, unguarded. Its line 432 routes float to int64 to uint32 and the comment there claims that makes it well defined; it does for finite floats below `2^63`, but `static_cast` of `±inf`, `NaN`, or anything at or above `2^63` is still undefined. **A second, separate bug in one of those lines.** `pad_rm_sharded_width_only_program_factory.cpp:120` routes INT32 and UINT32 through one `uint32_t` cast, destroying every negative int32 pad: `-1.0f` must reach the kernel as `0xFFFFFFFF` and only the signed conversion produces that. Line 116 of the same file already calls a guarded `float_to_uint16()` for UINT16, and the tilize helper already splits the two correctly, so the pattern is in the adjacent branch. ### The target behaviour, which the repository already specifies Saturate. Host float-to-integer semantics are stated as clamping in four places, all of which I checked against the boundary values: `ttnn/ttnn/operations/core.py:610-630`, the `_ttnn_is_host` arms of `_typecast_golden_function`, truncating then clamping for uint8, uint16 and uint32; `core.py:247-249`, the `from_torch` golden, commented *"Host float-to-uint16 conversion truncates and clamps"*; `golden_generators.py:1944-1951`, clamping uint16, uint32 and int32, whose `saturate_integer` helper is documented *"Hardware saturates (clamps) values instead of wrapping on overflow"*; and `tests/ttnn/unit_tests/base_functionality/test_comparison_mode.py:216-225`, which already asserts that a host `-1.0` bfloat16 to uint8 is `0`. Rejecting instead would not work for `ttnn.pad`: its signature takes a `float`, and **`INT32_MAX` and `UINT32_MAX` are not float-representable.** The nearest floats, `2^31` and `2^32`, are out of range, so a range check would make `ttnn.pad(int32_tensor, value=2147483647)` fail with `TT_FATAL` and leave the API unable to name its own extremes. `to_layout_op.cpp:205-218` can afford to reject only because it converts into the `uint32_t` arm of `PadValue` itself. The honest cost: `ttnn.pad(uint32_tensor, value=-1)` becomes a deterministic `0` on both architectures, where x86_64 wrote `0xFFFFFFFF`. `-1` was never a portable spelling of that sentinel; the portable spelling is the `uint32_t` arm of `PadValue`, which `fill_pad` and `tilize_with_val_padding` accept and `ttnn.pad` should grow. ### It is not only cross-architecture. It is cross-optimization-level on one machine. Found while writing the fix. **GCC constant-folds an out-of-range float-to-integer conversion to the saturating answer, while the aarch64 instruction it emits for the same expression wraps.** Reproduced on gcc 12.5.0 and 13.x, and at `-O0` as well as `-O2`: the operative variable is whether the operand is a compile-time literal, not the version or the optimization level. `(uint16_t)65536.0f` folds to `65535` at compile time and computes `0` at run time on the same machine with the same compiler. So the value depends on whether the conversion survives to run time, which depends on whether the operand is visible to the optimizer. At `-O2` on aarch64 the folded form compiles to `mov w0, -1; ret`, with no floating-point instruction at all, while the `volatile` form emits `fcvtzu` and computes `0`. Any test written without forcing the conversion to run time will pass against the unpatched code and prove nothing. The tests for this had to read the value back through a `volatile` for that reason. ### Which architectures Both. ARM host support is a live, merged goal rather than an aspiration, which is why I am filing this as a bug and not a feature request: PRs #20980 "Enable aarch64" and #44763 "ci: add aarch64 native Ubuntu 24.04 build workflow" are merged, #43940 guards x86 cache-flush intrinsics for aarch64, `cmake/aarch64-linux-clang-20-libstdcpp-toolchain.cmake` is in tree, and ttsim and SFPI both ship aarch64 artifacts. ### How it was verified The lambda from `tensor_apis.cpp:484` compiled verbatim and run **natively** on aarch64 Ubuntu 24.04. The x86_64 column is gcc 12.5 in a `linux/amd64` container on that same aarch64 host, so it is **emulated x86 rather than native**, and I would rather label it than let it pass as a hardware measurement. The values match the documented `cvttss2si` behaviour, which returns the integer indefinite value `0x80000000` for any source outside the destination range including `±inf` and NaN, so I expect them to hold on real hardware, but I have not run them there. torch 2.9.1 on aarch64 confirmed the reference values. The device column is read from source and not executed. ### What is already reported, and what is not **The `fill_pad` arms are half-covered and I am flagging it rather than letting a reviewer find it.** **#42004** (closed 2026-04-14) reported this identical mechanism at this identical file, caught by UBSan: *"The `static_cast(-inf)` on line 55 is undefined behavior per the C++ standard."* **PR #42005** fixed it same-day by moving the cast into an `else` branch so float destinations no longer take it, and **the raw casts for the integer destinations survive at HEAD.** Those are what this covers. If that reads as the same bug rather than the arms #42005 left behind, say so and I will withdraw that part. **#44604** (open) already proposes the `PadValue` extension recommended below, on NaN-payload grounds rather than undefined behaviour, naming the same files. The remedies coincide. **#55684** (open, filed today) reports the binary twin of the `ternary_op_utils.cpp` site but frames it as fractional truncation and proposes dtype promotion, so the out-of-range case is untouched there too. Four live artefacts quote the pad factories' packing block while fixing only the adjacent FLOAT32 branch: #54223, bot PR #54246, PR #54375, and PR #52326. `tensor_apis.cpp:484` itself is unreported. **#21915**, *"Fix on-host to_dtype op"*, read in full with its comments, is five cleanup items about file layout, test coverage, duplication and an untilize bug, pointing at the old `to_dtype_op.hpp` location, and says nothing about range or undefined behaviour. **#51655** names the same line as *"a `static_cast`, and C++ float-to-integral conversion discards the fractional part"*, reporting the truncation as correct reference semantics rather than the UB. ### Prior art Searched full text for `static_cast int overflow`, `float to int conversion`, `INT_MIN saturate`, `char signedness`, `undefined behavior golden`, `typecast overflow` and `host device mismatch typecast`: all empty. Read in full rather than by title: **#41537**, the `std::clamp` golden-UB find, the same technique at a different site, closed in a day; **#51476**, INT32_MIN in div, device side; **#21915**, *"Fix on-host to_dtype op"*, a cleanup ticket listing poor test coverage that says nothing about overflow or UB. Eight more read and ruled out: #51227, #16279, #31395, #17159, #28545, #27746, #15699, #54854. Nothing covers this. ## Repro, host only, no device needed ```cpp // g++ -O2 -o probe probe.cpp && ./probe #include #include #include // verbatim from tt_metal/impl/tensor/tensor_apis.cpp:484 template Dst convert(Src value) { return static_cast(value); } int main() { // volatile so the conversion survives to run time; see the folding note above volatile float a = 1e30f, b = std::numeric_limits::quiet_NaN(); volatile float c = std::numeric_limits::infinity(), d = -1.0f, e = -3e9f; printf("1e30 -> int32 %d\n", convert(a)); printf("NaN -> int32 %d\n", convert(b)); printf("+inf -> uint32 %u\n", convert(c)); printf("-1.0 -> uint32 %u\n", convert(d)); printf("-3e9 -> uint32 %u\n", convert(e)); } ``` On x86_64 that prints `-2147483648`, `-2147483648`, `0`, `4294967295`, `1294967296`. On aarch64 it prints `2147483647`, `0`, `4294967295`, `0`, `0`. Neither matches the device on all five. The same divergence is visible through the public API without compiling anything, on a machine of each architecture: ```python import torch, ttnn x = torch.tensor([1e30, float("nan"), float("inf"), -1.0, -3e9], dtype=torch.float32) print(ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.int32))) print(ttnn.to_torch(ttnn.from_torch(x, dtype=ttnn.uint32))) ``` ## Validation, measured The fix widens to `double`, takes NaN out before the range test because it compares false against every bound, clamps to the destination bounds, then truncates. Same probe, same two architectures, before and after: | input | aarch64 before | aarch64 after | x86_64 before | x86_64 after | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **to int32** | | | | | | 1e30 | 2147483647 | 2147483647 | **-2147483648** | 2147483647 | | NaN | 0 | 0 | **-2147483648** | 0 | | +inf | 2147483647 | 2147483647 | **-2147483648** | 2147483647 | | FLT_MAX | 2147483647 | 2147483647 | **-2147483648** | 2147483647 | | 4.2e9 | 2147483647 | 2147483647 | **-2147483648** | 2147483647 | | -3e9 | -2147483648 | -2147483648 | -2147483648 | -2147483648 | | 3.7 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | | **to uint32** | | | | | | 1e30 | 4294967295 | 4294967295 | **0** | 4294967295 | | +inf | 4294967295 | 4294967295 | **0** | 4294967295 | | FLT_MAX | 4294967295 | 4294967295 | **0** | 4294967295 | | -1.0 | 0 | 0 | **4294967295** | 0 | | -3e9 | 0 | 0 | **1294967296** | 0 | | -100.0 | 0 | 0 | **4294967196** | 0 | | 4.2e9 | 4200000000 | 4200000000 | 4200000000 | 4200000000 | aarch64 native, gcc 11.5.0. The same probe also runs natively on macOS arm64 with clang and produces the aarch64 column exactly, so that half is confirmed on two unrelated aarch64 systems. The x86_64 column is gcc 12.5.0 in a `linux/amd64` container on the aarch64 host, so it is emulated; it matches the documented `cvttss2si` behaviour but has not been run on x86 hardware. **Before the change the two hosts disagree on five of nine rows for `int32` and six of nine for `uint32`. After it, all eighteen cells agree.** The aarch64 `int32` columns are worth reading on their own: `before` and `after` are identical there, because `fcvtzs` already saturates at that width. The patch changes only the cases that were wrong and leaves every case that was already right untouched, which is the property a reviewer should want and it is visible in the table rather than asserted. In-range values are unaffected on both, `3.7` truncating to `3` and `-100.0` to `-100`, so this is not a rounding change. ## Acceptance criteria 1. `to_dtype` and everything routed through it converts out-of-range floats identically on x86_64 and aarch64, and matches the device. 2. The rule is saturation, matching `torch.Tensor.to()` and the four golden sites above: values at or beyond a bound clamp to it, and NaN goes to `0`. 3. All seven `ttnn.pad` factories change together, so an out-of-range pad no longer depends on the tensor's memory layout. The quasar mirror follows or is tracked separately. 4. `pad_rm_sharded_width_only_program_factory.cpp:120` stops routing INT32 through a `uint32_t` cast, so a negative int32 pad survives. 5. Tests cover the boundaries at `2^31`, `2^32`, `±inf`, `NaN` and `-1.0` into every unsigned destination, and **force the conversion to run time**, since a literal operand is constant-folded to the saturating answer and would pass against unpatched code. 6. Whether `ttnn.pad` grows a `uint32_t` arm on `PadValue`, so a bit-pattern sentinel can be expressed portably, is settled. #44604 already proposes this on other grounds. ## What I have A patch for `tensor_apis.cpp` and the pad sites, adding a `tt::saturating_cast` in `tt_metal/api/tt-metalium/math.hpp` built on the same widen-to-`double`-and-range-check shape as the existing `validate_float_pad_against_integral`. The ten tests that ship with it, six on host `to_dtype` and four on pad-value packing, are written but not yet run: this repository's build does not configure on the machine I have, which has no OpenSSL or Python development headers and no root. The call-site edits are reviewed rather than executed. What is executed is the helper itself, which is the part that decides every value the patch changes. Compiled standalone with gcc 13 at `-O0` and `-O2` on aarch64, and with gcc 12 on x86_64, it returns identical results on both architectures for all sixteen probes: `2^31`, `-2^31 - 1000`, `2^32`, `65536`, `256`, `-1.0`, `±inf` and NaN into int32, uint32, uint16 and uint8. Agreement across the two architectures is the whole point of the change, so that is the property I could most usefully verify without a build. On the scope question in acceptance criterion 3, I have since measured the answer rather than leaving it open. Six further factories carry the identical defect written as an **implicit** conversion, which is why a `static_cast` search does not surface them: ```cpp uint32_t packed_pad_value; // pad_value is `float` if (a.dtype() == DataType::INT32 || a.dtype() == DataType::UINT32) { packed_pad_value = pad_value; // float -> uint32_t, UB when out of range } ``` `pad_tile_multicore_program_factory.cpp:100`, `pad_tile_program_factory.cpp:86`, `pad_rm_reader_writer_program_factory.cpp:97`, `pad_rm_reader_writer_multi_core_program_factory.cpp:259`, `pad_rm_reader_writer_multi_core_default_program_factory.cpp:109`, `pad_rm_sharded_height_only_program_factory.cpp:341`. Routing INT32 through a `uint32_t` conversion destroys every negative int32 pad, not only out-of-range ones, since `-1.0f` has to reach the kernel as `0xFFFFFFFF` and only the signed conversion produces that. `float_to_uint16` at `common.cpp:549` already saturates correctly and needs no change, and `tilize_with_val_padding_factory_helper.cpp:52` is integral-to-integral and is correctly left alone. So all seven pad factories need the same three-line split. I still have no hardware, so the device-side paths are unverified beyond source reading.
